_comment: Trust policy for edullm-reservoir-ingest — WHO may become this role.
`ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com` and nothing else. AWS Batch runs its containers as ECS tasks, so
that service principal is what a running job needs; no human session, no other role, and no
EC2 instance can assume it. Same shape as the validator and the prm800k roles, verified live
WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. The intern role in this account carries
AdministratorAccess, so IAM is not what keeps a human out of the pipeline's identities — this
trust policy is. It is also why the airlock's delete Deny could not be probed AS the validator
during the v2 deployment: no session can assume that role, which is the invariant working.
Deliberately NO `Condition` block. A SourceArn condition scoping this to one job queue looks
stronger and is a footgun: Batch does not populate `aws:SourceArn` on the ECS task-assume call
the way one would expect, so the condition would evaluate false and every job would fail to
start with an unhelpful credential error. The blast radius is already bounded by the
permission policy (08-reservoir-ingest-policy.json), which grants no write to edullm-data.
